data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Italy’s Officine Gullo , a manufacturer of luxury commercial and residential kitchens, has taken 3,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at Sunlight Development ’s 95 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned.

Got Your Six , a licensed dispensary based in New Jersey, has signed a 2,300-square-foot lease at 256 West Street , also known as 92 Laight Street .

NBA Store Seeks New, Larger Location Up to 25K Square Feet: Jump ball. The NBA Store, which is operated by Fanatics -owned sports apparel company Lids , is planning to relocate from its longtime retail location at 545 Fifth Avenue into a larger space, Commercial Observer can first report.

Carnegie Diner & Cafe Operator to Open New Restaurant at 7 Penn Plaza: Carnegie Hospitality is opening its next Carnegie Diner & Cafe in Manhattan’s Penn District. The restaurateur signed on the dotted line last month to take over fast-casual chain Smashburger ’s lease at the Feil Organization ’s 7 Penn Plaza , Commercial Observer has learned.

items.headline: Institutions Turn to JVs for Grocery-Anchored Retail
items.summary: Institutional investors are using joint ventures to gain exposure to retail, especially grocery-anchored centers, citing supply-and-demand fundamentals and long-term income growth. Investors want experienced operators with leasing, tenant-mix and local-market know-how, while operators get capital in return for acquisitions, development and redevelopment. JV equity is still hard to raise amid high rates, valuation uncertainty and buyer-seller gaps, so some investors are buying stakes in operating companies instead.…

items.headline: Grocery-Anchored Retail Premium Hinges on Store and Lease
items.summary: Grocery-anchored retail is among the most competitive investment niches, with 2025 transaction volume near $11B and cap rates averaging 6.7%, but the grocery label alone doesn’t justify a premium. Buyers should study store sales, the grocer’s competitive position and remodel plans, plus lease terms such as sales-based termination rights, co-tenancy clauses and replacement restrictions.…

items.headline: Got Your Six Cannabis Dispensary Secures Manhattan Flagship
items.summary: A cannabis store is opening its Manhattan flagship location at the base of a luxury Tribeca condominium building. Got Your Six , a licensed dispensary based in New Jersey, has signed a 2,300-square-foot lease at 256 West Street , also known as 92 Laight Street . The corner retail lease between Laight and Vestry streets occupies part of the ground floor at Riverloft Condominiums , a 13-story luxury complex, and is near Hudson River Park . Crain’s New York first reported on the deal.…

items.headline: Carnegie Diner & Cafe Operator to Open New Restaurant at 7 Penn Plaza
items.summary: Carnegie Hospitality is opening its next Carnegie Diner & Cafe in Manhattan’s Penn District. The restaurateur signed on the dotted line last month to take over fast-casual chain Smashburger ’s lease at the Feil Organization ’s 7 Penn Plaza , Commercial Observer has learned. The tri-party deal included a 10-year lease extension for the 5,609-square-foot retail space at the corner of Seventh Avenue and West 31st Street.…

items.headline: Mexican Eatery Casa Carmen to Open Third Manhattan Location
items.summary: Mexican restaurant Casa Carmen is opening its third Manhattan location in Midtown East, Commercial Observer has learned. The restaurant concept started by chef Carmen “Titita” Ramírez Degollado signed a 15-year, 6,917-square-foot lease to serve up traditional Mexican cuisine at Sage ’s 437 Madison Avenue , according to tenant broker Retail by MONA as well as the landlord . Asking rent for the space was $200 per square foot, according to Retail by MONA.…

items.headline: PSP and Nuveen Launch $790M Grocery-Anchored Retail JV
items.summary: PSP Investments and Nuveen Real Estate launched a joint venture with an initial $790M to buy open-air shopping centers anchored by grocers, necessity retailers and essential services. The partners have closed about 3M SF across 19 properties in eight states, including two portfolios of six centers (801,000 SF) and 11 properties (1.9M SF). PSP says it is narrowing U.S. retail exposure to grocery-anchored centers that deliver inflation-linked income, a bet on daily-needs tenants and high-barrier metros.…

items.headline: Financial Tech Platform Intuit Takes 4K SF at the Orchard in LIC
items.summary: The Orchard , Queens’ tallest residential tower, has signed several new retail leases totaling 7,468 square feet, building owner and developer BLDG Management announced Thursday. In September, financial services platform Intuit , the company behind programs including TurboTax , QuickBooks , Credit Karma and Mailchimp , signed a 3,546-square-foot lease at the 70-story property at 42-06 Orchard Street in Queens’ Long Island City neighborhood.…

items.summary: Younger Partners Investments bought Crossroads at Terrell, a fully leased 260,876 SF power center 30 miles east of Dallas, from RealtyLink for an undisclosed price. A regional bank’s senior loan and preferred equity from a national REIT financed the deal, and the center ranked as Texas’ third most-visited retail destination in 2025, per Placer.ai.…

items.headline: Retail Starts Hit a 10-Year Low as Pipeline Falls to 58.3M SF
items.summary: CoStar says 58.3M SF of retail was under construction in Q3, down from 60.6M SF in Q2 and 63.3M SF in Q1, roughly 4% under the 10-year average of 60.7M SF. New starts totaled about 7.7M SF, down from 10.7M SF in Q2 and the lowest quarterly figure since at least 2016, as elevated land, construction and borrowing costs strain feasibility. Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston and Austin hold nearly 27% of the national pipeline, and CoStar expects further shrinkage before any meaningful recovery.…

items.headline: Banks Lock Up Manhattan Retail Space as Availability Hits Low
items.summary: Bank of America took 16,000 square feet at 19 Union Square West and Citibank took 14,000 square feet at 170 West 72nd Street, two of Manhattan’s largest third-quarter retail leases. Most bank activity is renewals and strategic relocations by existing tenants, and banks are returning to corner locations in a market where space is hard to replace. Prime corridor availability fell to a record-low 157 spaces, and one JLL broker has five or six more bank deals in progress, a sign of broader retail strength.…

items.headline: Hudson Valley Boutique Shop Signs Lease in Manhattan’s Nolita
items.summary: A Beacon, N.Y., knickknack shop is making its New York City debut with a store in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Solstad House General Store signed a five-year, 1,200-square-foot lease at Emmanuel Stark ’s 167 Mott Street , with an asking rent of $6,750 per month, according to broker Meridian Retail Leasing .…

items.headline: Fintech Firm Octaura Holdings Inks 29K SF at ESRT’s 111 West 33rd Street
items.summary: Octaura Holdings , an electronic trading, data and analytics provider, is moving its offices to 111 West 33rd Street near Midtown Manhattan’s Herald Square . The 28,914-square-foot deal with Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) spans the entire 17th floor of the 26-story office building, the landlord announced Monday. Octaura currently lists its Manhattan headquarters at Haymes Investment Company ’s 5 Penn Plaza , but it was not immediately clear whether the company intends to depart that space.…

items.headline: Catalyst IOS Doubles HQ at SL Green’s 800 Third Avenue to 12K SF
items.summary: Catalyst IOS , an investment manager specializing in industrial outdoor storage (IOS), has doubled the size of its 800 Third Avenue headquarters, Commercial Observer has learned. Catalyst’s new 12,000-square-foot office takes up the entire 35th floor of SL Green Realty ’s Midtown East Manhattan tower. The company will move from its current 6,000-square-foot space on the 27th floor, according to a company spokesperson. The deal carries a five-year term, and the asking rent was not disclosed.…

items.headline: Architecture Firm Corgan Expands to 41K SF at Empire State Building
items.summary: Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) signed more than 28,600 square feet of leases at the Empire State Building in the third quarter of this year. In the largest deal, architecture firm Corgan signed a 12.4-year, 15,157-square-foot lease in the building in an expansion from its current 26,035 square feet, giving it a total footprint of 41,192 square feet at the landmarked office building, according to ESRT’s third-quarter earnings report .…

items.headline: Life Time Inks 20-Year Lease at Crescent Heights’ Miami Dev Site
items.summary: Health club chain Life Time is coming to Miami’s Edgewater neighborhood. The high-end gym operator, formerly known as Life Time Fitness, signed a 20-year lease at 3180 Biscayne Boulevard , a 2.6-acre, full-block development site owned by Crescent Heights , according to documents filed to Miami-Dade County. The gym will likely be part of a mixed-use development using the Live Local Act , a Florida law that grants developers faster approvals if at least 40 percent of units are priced as workforce housing.…

items.headline: Amazon’s Same-Day Delivery Expansion Reignites Demand for Last-Mile Logistics
items.summary: When Amazon makes moves in the delivery business, the entire retail industry tends to reorient itself around the e-commerce giant. So, when a September report from Business Insider revealed preliminary plans for Amazon to embark on a “ massive blitz in same-day delivery ” with a proposed expansion of facilities code-named Project Mercury, industrial real estate took notice.…

items.headline: Apparel Brand American Giant Leases Brooklyn Store at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue
items.summary: San Francisco-based apparel brand American Giant has arrived in Brooklyn. The manufacturer of sportswear and casual clothing made exclusively in the United States has signed a lease for 3,400 square feet at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue in North Williamsburg, where it will open its first Brooklyn store, according to a source familiar with the deal.…

items.headline: Day Care Operator Inks 21K-SF Lease in Brooklyn’s Gravesend
items.summary: A new Ukrainian day care, Ukrainian New Generation Kids Daycare , has signed a 21,000-square-foot lease at Yakov Ostrovsky ‘s 1940 Shore Parkway in Gravesend, Brooklyn. The day care center is expected to open in the entirety of the four-story commercial building in the second quarter of 2027, and will be able to accommodate 300 children, according to Ripco Real Estate , which represented both the landlord and the tenant in this deal. The length of the lease was not disclosed.…
